description: Lilly Christian Astrology original first edition 1647 printed CHAP CXI (editorial CXII), signs/face/hair/colour
original_primary_source: Wellcome Collection b30338724 original PDF frames 581–583, following context up to 586, physical sequence authoritative
authoring_scope: Original image grounded brief anchors/paraphrases, not a full diplomatic transcription. Highly qualified and potentially stigmatizing historic claims.

source_groups.scope: Printed chapter CXI start and Book I cross-reference

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXI / Nature of the Signes; Colour of the Face and Haire
claims.meaning_historical_only: The next standalone chapter begins below a divider on original frame 581; its subject combines sign-based body form with purported hair and facial colouring.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: This is sufficiently handled in our Introduction
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly explicitly refers readers to Book I, printed pages 93–99, instead of claiming these descriptions are independent new source findings.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Aries Taurus Libra Scorpio / moderate Stature
claims.meaning_historical_only: Aries, Taurus, Libra and Scorpio are grouped as moderate but somewhat taller stature; source categories are not measured heights.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Leo Virgo Sagittarius / Body more tall
claims.meaning_historical_only: Leo, Virgo and Sagittarius are grouped together as allegedly taller stature.
Cancer, Capricorn and Pisces are grouped together as allegedly shorter stature.
Gemini is assigned an indeterminate/intermediate stature category, not a precise height interval.
Aquarius is associated with moderate body proportion rather than a numeric height; distinguish proportions from the other stature bins.

source_groups.scope: Six separate sources for alleged colouring

claims.meaning_historical_only: The author's first testimony for colours is planets in the Ascendant, explicitly referring readers to his Book I pages 57–83 for planetary colour attributions.
The rising sign and an intercepted sign, where present, are separately named as colour testimonies.
Rulers of the rising/intercepted signs are additional testimonies; they are not interchangeable with planets physically in the first house.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Fourthly ... partilly beholding the degree ascending
claims.meaning_historical_only: Planets in partile aspect to the Ascendant degree or its ruler supply another condition; 'partile' is not an unconstrained aspect.
Fixed stars rising with the Ascendant are alleged to share colour indications attributed to planets of analogous nature.
The four traditional humours are used as another purported appearance source; this historical physiology is not a modern measurement.

source_groups.scope: Humour-based facial complexion claims and planetary conditions

claims.meaning_historical_only: The sanguine temperament receives a light/clear complexion stereotype in Lilly's historical classification.
Lilly assigns pallor to a phlegmatic temperament under the historical four-humour scheme; this is not modern physiology.
The choleric temperament is assigned yellow/red complexion, contrasting with other humours.
The melancholic temperament is assigned dark complexion within 17th-century humoral terminology; not a factual classification of people.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: one or both the Fortunes in the ascendant
claims.meaning_historical_only: Presence of one or both benefic planets at the Ascendant is described as improving appearance/colour judgments.
Lilly attributes unattractive appearance to both malefics at the Ascendant; this is an unverified, potentially stigmatizing stereotype.

source_groups.scope: Season, mixing, testimony tally and climate/country exception

claims.meaning_historical_only: The northern signs and additional named signs are connected to cheerful colouring; the complete glyph list needs further paleographic confirmation before formal sign-code transcription.
Winter signs and domiciles of the malefics are said to suggest a sadder appearance; do not convert expression into a psychological state prediction.
The printed text uses a four-colour base palette for the historical mixing procedure.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: all the rest come by mixture
claims.meaning_historical_only: Intermediate colours are described as mixtures of the four bases rather than new primitive categories.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Assigne to every Significator his severall colour
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly says to assign colours to each qualifying significator before combining judgments, rather than selecting a single symbol post hoc.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: according to the greater number so judge
claims.meaning_historical_only: A majority-of-testimonies instruction is given, but no calibrated measurement or conflict threshold is supplied.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: having judiciously framed a right mixture
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author allows a discretionary overall blending after the tally, creating considerable flexibility that future test design must freeze.
Lilly explicitly instructs accounting for local climate/country in any appearance judgment, contradicting a simple universal chart-only colouring rule.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if he be a Spaniard your judgment will faile
claims.meaning_historical_only: A Spain-based example admits that a purported fair-colour chart judgment may fail owing to place; the example reflects historical cultural stereotypes.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the Danes are faire or red-haired
claims.meaning_historical_only: Denmark-based stereotyped colouring is offered as a contrary geographic example; it provides neither validated ancestry inference nor independent predictive evidence.

source_groups.scope: Five factors of facial proportion and members

claims.meaning_historical_only: Both rising sign and Ascendant ruler are named as sources for facial and bodily proportions.
Planets and their configurations in relation to the Ascendant are separately mentioned.
Both luminaries constitute another source of face/member proportion testimonies.
Birth season is expressly counted as another variable; do not confuse it with weather affecting measured skin tone.
Stars rising with the Ascendant are cited as a fifth appearance factor, with no specified orb in this passage.

source_groups.scope: Humane signs and sign-group facial assessments

claims.meaning_historical_only: Human-form zodiac signs are linked to favorable/clear complexions; text includes the first part of Sagittarius and Aquarius, requiring position-specific interpretation.

Other named signs plus latter portions of Aries and Leo are linked to derogatory form stereotypes; the exact glyph sequence is visually delicate and should not be encoded as an unreviewed deterministic sign list.

source_groups.scope: Planetary testimony, afflicted states, and appearance/harm claims

claims.meaning_historical_only: Jupiter and Venus are favored in the source's subjective appearance judgments, not verified attractiveness predictors.
Mercury and Moon are secondary favorable appearance testimonies relative to Jupiter and Venus.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: yet if they be evill Planets ... ill Faces
claims.meaning_historical_only: The same planetary testimonies may be reversed according to unfavorable conditions; no unconditional benefic-only reading is justified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: when no way afflicted ... handsome Face
claims.meaning_historical_only: Absence of affliction is an explicit favorable qualifier, separate from mere planetary name.
Saturn, Mars and their adverse configurations to the Ascendant are blamed for unflattering appearance; a historically stigmatizing and unverified claim.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: an Infortune in the ascendant ... a Scarre
claims.meaning_historical_only: Saturn, Mars or the south lunar node at the Ascendant are alleged to mark facial scarring; not clinical or forensic evidence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Moon well dignified shew fairenesse
claims.meaning_historical_only: Well-dignified Sun/Moon are said to imply fairness, not a validated skin tone prediction.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: yet Sun gives proportion not pulchritude
claims.meaning_historical_only: The Sun is qualified as a form/proportion testimony rather than necessarily a beauty testimony.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Where the Lights are both impedited ... Eyes
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly associates impaired luminaries with eye harm, an unverified medical assertion.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Infortunes are joyned together ... deforme the Body
claims.meaning_historical_only: A complex, partly glyph-ambiguous malefic/light/latitude clause alleges bodily impairment and disease; preserve as authored history and do not promote to disability diagnosis.
Spring signs are alleged to produce attractive form, abundant/lovely hair and sanguine complexion.
Summer signs are described as bulkier, with medium height, abundant hair, large eyes and choleric complexion.
Autumn signs are said to indicate a lean body, spreading hair, fair eyes, moderate height and melancholic complexion.
Winter signs are linked to moderate bodily form, dark complexion, spread-but-thin hair and phlegmatic temperament.

source_groups.scope: Fixed stars, Mercury/Venus and the remaining stature qualification rules

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: fixed Starres assist in pulchritude or deformity
claims.meaning_historical_only: The nature of a fixed star's associated planet is said to modify favorable/negative appearance; this introduces another non-quantified testimony.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury or Venus ... Houses or Exaltations
claims.meaning_historical_only: Mercury or Venus in domicile/exaltation and aspecting the Ascendant is said to imply tall stature.
Their fall/detriment is treated as the contrary case, requiring separate dignity-state consideration.
Saturn, Jupiter and Mars in fall, detriment or retrograde are associated with medium-to-short height; this is an uncalibrated relative predicate.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: not Retrograde ... vary not the stature
claims.meaning_historical_only: An additional nonretrograde qualification restricts prior stature variation under fall/detriment, a conditional complication that should not be discarded.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If no Planet doe partilly behold the Lord
claims.meaning_historical_only: When no planet forms a partile aspect to the Ascendant ruler, its own state becomes the fallback for stature judgment.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Signe he is in not considered, if he be direct
claims.meaning_historical_only: A direct Ascendant ruler is treated differently from its sign-based retrograde/fall fallback; the exact grammatical scope should remain unresolved before executable coding.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If he be Retrograde and in his Fall
claims.meaning_historical_only: For a retrograde Ascendant ruler in fall, Lilly says to infer stature from the sign rather than the planet's own nature.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Luminaries having power and dignity in the Horoscope
claims.meaning_historical_only: When luminaries dominate the horoscope, stature is said to follow their zodiac sign.
If Mercury dominates the Ascendant, Lilly directs stature judgment through Mercury's dispositor, echoing the prior chapter and needing dependency deduplication.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXII Of the grossenesse or leannesse of Bodies
claims.meaning_historical_only: A separate numbered chapter begins below the divider on original frame 583; this heading is navigation, not an admitted sign/colour rule.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: after a full age, or about thirty yeers
claims.meaning_historical_only: The next chapter's opening restricts what it calls bulk or leanness to a mature-age condition; its complete method is left for the next batch.
